Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest radiograph (Figure 1b) demonstrates a distinct, dense curvilinear calcification outlining the anterior and inferior borders of the heart, which is the pathognomonic sign of constrictive calcified pericarditis. This finding correlates with the clinical history of a systolic murmur over the pulmonary valve, as pericardial constriction can lead to right-sided hemodynamic changes and functional murmurs.
